"This model will be a simplification and an idealization, and consequently a falsification. It is to be hoped that the features retained ***for discussion*** are those of greatest importance in the present state of knowledge." --Alan Turing

![](../images/Turing.jpg){width=100%}

"[We] treat the same problem with several alternative models each with different simplifications... if these models, despite their different assumptions, lead to similar results we have a robust theorem which is relatively free of the details of the model. Hence ***our truth is the intersection of independent lies.***" --Richard Levins

### Gray(t)-Scott! VisualPDE in a slide

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%}

::: {.column-text-spacing}
[VisualPDE Link](https://visualpde.com/nonlinear-physics/gray-scott.html){target="_blank"}
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%}
::: {.small}
$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} &= D_u\nabla^2 u + f(u,v) = \nabla^2 u +u^2 v - (a+b) u  \\
\frac{\partial v}{\partial t} &= D_v \nabla^2 v + g(u, v) = 2 \nabla^2 v-u^2 v + a (1 - v)
\end{aligned}
$$
:::
:::
:::

### Keller-Segel chemotaxis

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%}

::: {.column-text-spacing}
[VisualPDE Link](https://visualpde.com/sim/?preset=KellerSegel){target="_blank"}
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%}
::: {.small}
$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} &= D_u\nabla^2 u + \nabla \cdot (\chi(u,v)\nabla v) +u(1-u)  \\
\frac{\partial v}{\partial t} &= D_v \nabla^2 v + u-av
\end{aligned}
$$
:::
:::
:::

### Cyclic competition

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%}

::: {.column-text-spacing}
[VisualPDE Link](https://visualpde.com/mathematical-biology/cyclic-competition){target="_blank"}
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%}
::: {.small}
$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\partial u_i}{\partial t}&=D_{u_i}\nabla^2 u_i+u_i(1-u_i-au_{i-1}-bu_{i+1}) \\ &a < 1 < b, \quad i \in \{1,2,3\}\,\, (\textrm{mod } 3)
\end{aligned}
$$
:::
:::
:::

## Spatiotemporal heterogeneity 
$$
\frac{\partial \boldsymbol{u}}{\partial t} = \mathcal{L}(\nabla^2) \boldsymbol{u} + \boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{u}, p(\varepsilon x,\omega t)), \quad 0 < \varepsilon, \omega \ll 1.
$$

[![A patterned version of ALan Turing](../images/TuringPatterned.png){.nostretch fig-align="center" width="20%"}](https://visualpde.com/art-pdes/turing-face)


### Weakly nonlinear theory for spatiotemporal heterogeneity

...After some messy asymptotic calculations, we find that $\boldsymbol{u} = \boldsymbol{u_0} + \varepsilon A(\sigma, t) e^{i k_c x} \boldsymbol{U_1}$ where $A$ satisfies:
$$\begin{aligned}
        0 &=  \alpha_1\frac{\partial ^2 A}{\partial \sigma^2}   + \left(\dot{x_\ell}(t) \frac{\omega}{\varepsilon^8} \alpha_2 + i \alpha_{2,i}\right) \partial_\sigma A+ i \alpha_3 |A|^2 \partial_\sigma A
        \\
        &+ i \alpha_4 A^2 \overline{\partial_\sigma A} + \left(\alpha_5 + \sigma \partial_x p(x_\ell(t), t) \alpha_{5,s}\right) A + \alpha_6 |A|^2 A + \alpha_7 |A|^4 A.
\end{aligned}$$

::: {.fragment .fade-in-then-out}
![](../images/animation.gif)
:::
